bibliographic.title: From principles to practice: a novel matrix for evaluating AI-powered learning platforms based on the UNESCO Ethical Impact Assessment tool
bibliographic.authors: Rima J. Isaifan, Ayman Tawalbeh, Mazen O. Hasna
bibliographic.citation_apa: Isaifan, R. J., Tawalbeh, A., & Hasna, M. O. (2025). From principles to practice: a novel matrix for evaluating AI-powered learning platforms based on the UNESCO Ethical Impact Assessment tool. Frontiers in Education, 10, 1640780. https://doi.org/10.3389/feduc.2025.1640780

methodology.method_family: framework development and applied platform evaluation using UNESCO Ethical Impact Assessment operationalization
methodology.study_design: development of Gulf-AI Education Tool Evaluation Matrix (G-AIETM) applied to seven AI-powered educational platforms with 5-point Likert scoring and normalized rankings; actionable implementation framework for Khanmigo
methodology.sample_description: seven globally recognized AI-powered educational platforms: Khanmigo, CENTURY Tech, MATHia, Knewton Alta, AltSchool, Querium, and Squirrel AI
methodology.technology_context: AI-powered learning platforms including intelligent tutoring systems, NLP tools, predictive analytics, recommender systems, and Khanmigo powered by GPT technology; evaluation focused on ethical and pedagogical readiness in Gulf/Qatar education context

eligibility.decision_rationale: The study operationalizes UNESCO EIA into G-AIETM and evaluates ethical governance of AI educational platforms in a regulated education context, with Khanmigo noted as GPT-powered. It addresses accountability, transparency, data governance, compliance, and localization barriers relevant to governed AI deployment, but does not center conversational systems, chatbot governance, guardrails, observability, or LLM-specific operational controls.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Confirm whether Khanmigo's GPT-powered conversational features are evaluated beyond brief mention of adaptive interaction, and verify full-text coverage of governance mechanisms versus pedagogical localization.

appraisal.notes: Strengths include clear operationalization of UNESCO EIA into 18 indicators and structured scoring across seven platforms. Limitations visible in excerpt include reliance on publicly available documentation, small purposive platform sample, and limited detail on inter-rater reliability or validation of the adapted matrix.

cerqual.explanation: The framework and evaluation logic are coherent and explicitly tied to UNESCO EIA, but evidence is documentary and platform-scored rather than empirically tested in deployment. Relevance to conversational LLM governance is indirect: governance themes are strong, while conversational/LLM-specific operational governance is only partially evidenced.

coding.theme: Ethical governance and evaluation of AI-powered educational platforms
coding.subtheme: Operationalizing UNESCO EIA through a localized evaluation matrix
rq_alignment: partial alignment to LLM deployment governance

synthesis.main_claim: The authors propose G-AIETM as a structured adaptation of the UNESCO EIA Tool to evaluate AI-powered educational platforms against 18 ethical and pedagogical indicators, finding Khanmigo highest at 74.4% while all platforms require significant Arabic, cultural, and data-governance localization for Qatar.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a replicable, evidence-based evaluation matrix and implementation roadmap linking UNESCO ethical principles to practical platform assessment and localized deployment planning in Gulf education contexts.
synthesis.limitations: Evaluation depends on publicly available platform documentation; persistent barriers include resource limitations, regulatory gaps, insufficient Arabic support, and weak local compliance mechanisms across platforms.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on ethical governance frameworks and platform-level accountability/compliance evaluation in regulated education; not as central evidence for conversational LLM governance, guardrails, observability, or human oversight in dialogue systems.
